title: Neck cowl shawl hybrid
subtitle: A short wide rectangle in treble stitch with a picot border, worn as a neck scarf or draped shawl
excerpt: This DK-weight rectangle measures 130 cm wide by 30 cm deep and sits high on the shoulders, working equally well as a neck scarf, a looped cowl, or a small shawl. The body is worked in treble stitch on a 4 mm hook; a picot edging runs along all four sides. Finished size makes it a useful everyday piece that packs flat.
sourceNotes: Original pattern synthesised for Homemade. Treble rectangle construction with picot edge is a widely established technique with no single source.
heroPrompt: A short wide crochet rectangle in dusty rose DK yarn draped loosely around a person's neck and shoulders, photographed from the front in natural window light, with the picot edge clearly visible along the lower border.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small decorative loop on an edge formed by chaining 3, then working a slip stitch back into the base of the chain. Picots add a delicate sawtooth finish to a border.
The chain or chains worked at the start of a row to bring the hook to the correct height for the next row of stitches. For treble stitch a ch-3 turning chain counts as the first treble.

content.text: This rectangle works up quickly on a 4 mm hook in DK yarn and sits at the borderline between a neck scarf and a shawl. At 130 cm wide it will wrap once around the neck and still drape down the front, or lie flat across both shoulders with the ends tucked in. The treble body produces an open, lightly draped fabric; the picot border adds definition without bulk.
The construction is a plain rectangle: a foundation chain sets the width, then rows of treble build the depth. The
turning chain
counts as the first treble throughout, which keeps each row clean and even. The picot border is worked as a final round around all four sides once the rectangle is complete.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 200 g DK-weight yarn. A 4 mm crochet hook (US G/6). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Tape measure. Optional: blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Gauge

18 tr x 10 rows = 10 x 10 cm in DK yarn with a 4 mm hook, measured unstretched. Work a swatch of at least 24 stitches and 14 rows, then measure the central 10 x 10 cm area. Adjust hook size if needed: one stitch per 10 cm off the stated gauge changes the finished width by about 7 cm.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
picot
: ch 3, sl st into base of chain.
Pattern

The rectangle is worked flat in rows. The ch-3 turning chain at the start of every row counts as the first treble. Do not work into the top of that turning chain on the following row. Skip it and work the last stitch of every row into the top of the previous row's turning chain.
Foundation chain
Ch 238. (This becomes 235 trebles after the first row, which gives 130 cm at the stated gauge.)
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in the 4th ch from hook. 1 tr in each remaining ch. Turn. (235 sts)
Rows 2 to 30
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in each st across, working the final tr into the top of the turning ch from the previous row. Turn. (235 sts)
After Row 30, the rectangle measures approximately 130 cm x 30 cm. Do not fasten off.
Picot border
Work the picot border as a continuous round around all four edges. The sequence at corners allows the work to turn without puckering.

Round 1: do not turn. Join yarn at the top right corner. Work 1 dc (UK double crochet, the same move as US single crochet) into each stitch along the top edge to the corner. At each corner work (1 dc, ch 2, 1 dc) into the corner stitch. Continue down the short right side, working 1 dc into each row-end. Repeat along the bottom edge and up the short left side. Join with sl st to the first dc.

Round 2 (picot round): *1 dc in next dc, ch 3, sl st back into base of ch (1 picot made), 1 dc in each of next 2 dc*; repeat from * to * all the way round. At each corner chain space, work (1 dc, ch 3, sl st, 1 dc). Join with sl st. Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends securely through the backs of several stitches in different directions. Wet-block by soaking the finished piece in cool water for 10 minutes, gently pressing out excess water in a towel, then pinning to the finished dimensions on a blocking mat. Leave until completely dry before unpinning.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild wool wash. Lay flat to dry. Do not tumble-dry or hang while wet.
What to try next

Work the same rectangle in a sport-weight linen blend on a 3.5 mm hook for a lighter summer version. Replace the plain treble body with a V-stitch (tr, ch 1, tr into the same st) for a more open mesh. A contrast colour picot border in a second DK shade gives a clean, two-tone finish.
